blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At enterprise scale, taxpayer obligations multiply dramatically. A single group may hold dozens of legal entities, each a taxpayer in its own right, each with its own filings, its own deadlines, and its own relationship with a local tax authority. The senior leader's job is to make sure this whole portfolio moves in step — without reducing it to a centralised bureaucracy that local teams cannot work with.

The discipline rests on a few simple rules. Every entity has a named tax owner. Every obligation must be tracked on a single master calendar visible to the centre. Every unusual position must be approved in principle by the central team before the local entity commits to it. Local teams keep the initiative; the centre keeps the coherence.

When this is done well, a global group can file hundreds of returns a year across dozens of jurisdictions without any of them becoming newsworthy. That quiet scale is one of the silent signatures of senior finance leadership.

items.q: According to the text, why do taxpayer obligations multiply at enterprise scale?
options: Because each legal entity is a taxpayer in its own right, with its own filings and deadlines
Because central teams duplicate the work of local ones
Because tax rates rise as a group grows larger
Because regulators demand a single consolidated return
items.why: "each a taxpayer in its own right, each with its own filings, its own deadlines" — cada entidade traz suas próprias obrigações.

items.q: What does the author say the senior leader must avoid when coordinating the portfolio?
options: Making obligations visible on a master calendar
Reducing the group to a centralised bureaucracy that local teams cannot work with
Naming a tax owner for each entity
Approving unusual positions in principle
items.why: "without reducing it to a centralised bureaucracy that local teams cannot work with."

items.q: How does the text describe the balance of control between the centre and local teams?
options: The centre owns every decision; local teams only execute
The centre withdraws entirely once rules are set
Local teams keep the initiative while the centre keeps the coherence
Local teams and the centre share every filing equally
items.why: "Local teams keep the initiative; the centre keeps the coherence."

items.q: The phrase "without any of them becoming newsworthy" suggests that, at this scale, success looks like…
options: obligations handled so cleanly that they attract no attention
regular coverage in the financial press
public recognition for the finance team
a reduction in the number of returns filed
items.why: Inferência: "quiet scale" e "silent signatures" — a excelência aqui é justamente não virar notícia.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Coordinating a portfolio of entities requires shared visibility
Unusual positions deserve central review before a commitment is made
Local teams should retain the initiative in their own jurisdictions
Centralising everything into one bureaucracy is the safest way to control obligations
items.why: Inferência: o texto adverte explicitamente contra a burocracia centralizada — coerência sim, centralização total não.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver apresentando o novo modelo de obrigações à liderança financeira. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me set out where we've landed. We've got twenty-two entities across fourteen jurisdictions, and until now each one has managed its own obligations in its own way. That has to change — not by taking the work away from the local teams, but by making all of it visible in one place.

So here's the shape of it. Every entity is being given a named tax owner. That owner stays local — they know the authority, they know the deadlines. What's new is that every obligation must now be logged on a single master calendar that the centre can see. Nothing should sit in someone's inbox or their head anymore.

There's one rule I want to be firm about. If an entity is about to take an unusual position — something aggressive, something novel — it must be cleared in principle with the central team before anyone commits to it locally. Not because we don't trust you, but because a surprise in one jurisdiction can very quickly become a problem for the whole group.

Handled this way, we should be able to file several hundred returns a year and never once end up in the papers. That's the whole point. Quiet is what good looks like here.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many entities and jurisdictions is Oliver's framework covering?
options: Twelve entities across four jurisdictions
Twenty-two entities across fourteen jurisdictions
Fourteen entities across twenty-two jurisdictions
Twenty entities across ten jurisdictions
items.why: "twenty-two entities across fourteen jurisdictions."

items.q: According to Oliver, where does the named tax owner sit?
options: With an external advisory firm
Rotating between jurisdictions each quarter
In the central team at head office
Locally, close to the authority and the deadlines
items.why: "That owner stays local — they know the authority, they know the deadlines."

items.q: What must happen before an entity takes an unusual position?
options: It must be announced to all other entities
It must be cleared in principle with the central team first
It must be filed and then reviewed afterwards
It must be approved by the local tax authority
items.why: "it must be cleared in principle with the central team before anyone commits to it locally."

items.q: When Oliver says "Nothing should sit in someone's inbox or their head anymore," he most likely means that…
options: staff should stop using email entirely
the central team will take over every filing
local teams should no longer manage their own deadlines
obligations must be captured in a shared, visible system rather than held informally
items.why: Inferência: o ponto é tornar tudo rastreável no calendário mestre, não deixar informação dispersa e invisível.

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "Quiet is what good looks like here"?
options: Success is measured by obligations handled so smoothly they attract no attention
The group should reduce how many returns it files
Returns should be filed late to avoid scrutiny
The team should communicate less with each other
items.why: Inferência: filing centenas de declarações "and never once end up in the papers" — a excelência é invisível.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Each subsidiary is a separate legal entity, so its returns cannot be merged with the parent's." A legal entity is…
options: a department within a single company
a member of the finance leadership team
a written contract between two firms
an organisation recognised in law as a taxpayer in its own right
items.why: Legal entity = entidade jurídica, reconhecida em lei e responsável por suas próprias obrigações.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The team missed the deadline, so the ___ was submitted late and triggered a penalty."
options: portfolio
filing
coherence
initiative
items.why: Filing = declaração/entrega às autoridades — é o que foi submetido em atraso.

items.q: "An unusual position should be approved in principle before the entity commits to it." In principle here means…
options: signed and legally binding
agreed as an idea, before the details are finalised
rejected outright
postponed indefinitely
items.why: In principle = em princípio: acordo sobre a ideia, ainda sem fechar todos os detalhes.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We need one ___ that the centre can see, listing every deadline across all fourteen jurisdictions."
options: bureaucracy
master calendar
local tax authority
legal entity
items.why: Master calendar = calendário mestre, a visão única de todos os prazos.

items.q: "Local teams keep the initiative; the centre keeps the coherence." Coherence here means…
options: the consistency that keeps the whole portfolio aligned
the number of jurisdictions involved
the size of the central team
the speed of each local filing
items.why: Coherence = coerência: a consistência que mantém o conjunto alinhado enquanto o local mantém a iniciativa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de compliance fiscal. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The group tax director still has to sign off on any aggressive position." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
quietly ignore
comment informally
publicly announce
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the master calendar jurisdiction by jurisdiction." To roll out means to…
options: wind down gradually
implement in stages
test in secret
escalate to the board
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "Two local controllers pushed back on the central sign-off rule." They…
options: resisted or objected to it
rewrote the whole framework
forgot about it
adopted it enthusiastically
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar por completo.

items.q: "The entity agreed to log its deadlines but never followed through." It…
options: changed jurisdictions midway
documented it in detail
delegated the task to the centre
failed to carry the commitment to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A late filing can quickly snowball into compounding penalties." To snowball into means to…
options: grow rapidly into something much larger
be resolved without cost
disappear over time
be capped at a fixed amount
items.why: Snowball into = crescer rápido, como bola de neve — reflete a advertência de que penalidades compõem rapidamente.
